shared_elements: tall upright anthropomorphic pillar/stela with carving on its broad front face
upper register of repeated relief motifs arranged in a row across the top block
arch-like / loop-shaped repeated forms in the top register
circular or disc motif on the body
horizontal band with chevron/zigzag or repeated-stroke pattern crossing the shaft (belt-like)
schematic bent limbs/arms rendered in low relief on the front
small animal or creature figures in relief
justification: Both surfaces present a monolithic upright anthropomorphic body carved in shallow relief with the same vertical scheme: a row of repeated, arch-like/looped motifs across the top register, then bent limbs and a disc or rounded motif on the torso, then a horizontal belt-like band filled with chevron or repeated-stroke pattern, with smaller creature forms below. The biggest differences in content are that B's upper register is clearly populated by identifiable animals and hands with elongated fingers meeting at the belt, while A's motifs are heavier, bulbous and more abstract (a prominent ringed disc as a pectoral and mask-like head-zone bands), so the specific inventory of creatures and attributes does not match closely.
